headline: England Test captain Ben Stokes to retire from international cricket
summary: The 35-year-old talisman, known for his fearless batting and 2019 World Cup triumph, will step down after the current Test against New Zealand.
details: England Test captain Ben Stokes has announced his retirement from international cricket. He will step down following the ongoing Test match against New Zealand at Trent Bridge.
The 35-year-old made his international debut in 2011 and has led England's Test team since 2022. His announcement at Trent Bridge was met with a standing ovation from the crowd.
Stokes is celebrated for his role in England's 2019 50-over World Cup victory, where he scored an unbeaten 84 in the final. He is widely regarded as one of the defining figures of his generation.
One of his most iconic moments was the unbeaten 135 at Headingley in 2019, guiding England to a one-wicket win over Australia after being bowled out for 67 in the first innings.
ECB chair Richard Thompson praised Stokes as one of England's greatest ever cricketers, citing his relentless competitiveness and ability to produce extraordinary results under pressure.
caption:

headline_marked: Sheikh Hasina says [[she will return to Bangladesh this year]]
headline: Sheikh Hasina says she will return to Bangladesh this year
summary: In an exclusive interview with NDTV, the former prime minister rejected a death sentence against her as politically motivated and vowed to return to her country.
details: Former prime minister Sheikh Hasina has announced her intention to return to Bangladesh before the end of the year, despite facing a death sentence and a ban on the Awami League's political activities.
In an exclusive interview with NDTV, she described the verdict against her as part of an "illegal, unconstitutional, and politically motivated process" designed to leave the Awami League leaderless.
Hasina stated that her return is not driven by personal ambition, but by a struggle to restore democracy, the rule of law, and the political rights of the people of Bangladesh.
She argued that the Awami League's strength lies in its history and grassroots organization, claiming that political persecution has only made the party stronger.
The former premier also alleged that democracy and public security have deteriorated under the current leadership, while extremism has spread and minority communities have come under pressure.
Marking the party's 77th founding anniversary on June 23, Hasina urged supporters to remain united and defend the rights of marginalized communities, women, and children.
caption:
Despite a death sentence and a party ban, Sheikh Hasina vows to return to Bangladesh this year.

Former prime minister Sheikh Hasina has announced her intention to return to Bangladesh before the end of the year, despite facing a death sentence and a ban on the Awami League's political activities.

In an exclusive interview with NDTV, she described the verdict against her as part of an "illegal, unconstitutional, and politically motivated process" designed to leave the Awami League leaderless.

Hasina stated that her return is not driven by personal ambition, but by a struggle to restore democracy, the rule of law, and the political rights of the people of Bangladesh.

She argued that the Awami League's strength lies in its history and grassroots organization, claiming that political persecution has only made the party stronger.

The former premier also alleged that democracy and public security have deteriorated under the current leadership, while extremism has spread and minority communities have come under pressure.

Marking the party's 77th founding anniversary on June 23, Hasina urged supporters to remain united and defend the rights of marginalized communities, women, and children.
